title: Reading your shop's own state
target: The state a Supermarket Simulator shop keeps about itself — its status, its ground, its doors and the crowd inside — so what the shop is doing can be read rather than sensed.
version: 1.6.0 (223), read from the copy of the game this site was built from (see the sources page)
prerequisites: A shop open for the day

steps.do: Expect the shop itself to have a status.
steps.because: the shop has a status of its own, with an interaction built around it (StoreStatus, StoreStatusInteraction)

steps.do: Know that the walkable ground is prepared for you.
steps.because: there is a navigation mesh for the shop, so the walkable ground is prepared (StoreNavmesh)
there is a door into the store and a door of the market's own (DoorToStore, LocalMarketDoor)

steps.do: Read the door switch's overlay rather than hunting for a handle.
steps.because: a door switch has an overlay of its own (DoorSwitchOverlay)

steps.do: Expect the market side to have its own controllers, including its lights.
steps.because: the market's store is held by a controller with a networked version, and the market's lights have a controller of their own (NetworkLocalMarketStoreController, MarketLightsController)

steps.do: Expect customers to be produced rather than to be a fixed cast.
steps.because: customers are produced by a generator and how many arrive is governed by a spawn setting of its own (CustomerGenerator, CustomerSpawnSettingSO)

steps.do: Recognise the crowd as a set of models rather than one shopper repeated.
steps.because: the crowd is drawn from a set of character models the game ships (BusinessMan_Jacket_MAT_AlbedoTransparency_V3, UrbanGuy_B_Body_MAT_AlbedoTransparency_V1)

steps.do: Listen to the customers as data rather than as noise.
steps.because: customer speech is data of its own with a list of entries, sorted into kinds, and a customer's name is drawn on a board of its own (CustomerSpeech, CustomerSpeechEntry, CustomerSpeechType, CustomerNameBilboard)

commonMistakes: Treating the shop as a room rather than as an object with a status.
Confusing the store door with the market's own door.
Expecting the same customers every day.
Reading a name board as decoration rather than as the customer's own name.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. Grounding for each step is on the technical reference pages; no number is estimated.
